options: Some orders made to order, some from stock

questions.text: How do you track an order from enquiry to dispatch?
How many Excel sheets does your team update every week?
How often do delivery dates slip, or stock surprise you?
A customer asks “Where is my order?” How long does it take to answer?
How quickly can you see today’s sales, dues and stock?
options: Only when the accountant prepares it

questions.text: If a figure is changed, can you see who changed it and when?
What are your biggest headaches right now?

firefighting: Your business runs on people’s effort and memory. It works, but it is tiring, and it limits how fast you can grow.
partly: Some systems are in place, but the gaps between them still cost time and bring surprises.
in_control: You have a good grip. The gains from here are in fine-tuning and visibility.

q2: Put every order on one screen
When orders live in Excel and WhatsApp, the latest status sits in someone’s head. One screen from enquiry to dispatch lets anyone see where an order stands.
Sales, work orders and dispatch in one place, with promised and actual dates.
q3: Retire the spreadsheets one by one
Every extra sheet is another version of the truth, and someone’s evening spent matching them up. Start with the sheet that is updated most often.
Orders, stock, purchase and production in one system, so the sheets are no longer needed.
q4: Plan against real capacity and stock
Most slipped dates are promised before anyone checks machines and material. Check both before a date is given.
Production planning and material readiness for every work order, with Predictive & order outlook.
q5: Answer “Where is my order?” in seconds
If the answer needs three phone calls, the customer feels it. Give everyone the same live status.
Live order and dispatch status, with dispatch release sign-off.
q6: Decisions made on last month’s figures are guesses. A short daily look at sales, dues and stock changes how the week is run.
Live views of sales, receivables, payables and stock.
q7: Know who changed what, and when
When a figure changes without a trace, trust goes with it. A record of every change settles questions in minutes.
An audit log of every change, with roles and approvals.
h_dispatch: Fix a daily dispatch plan from confirmed stock, and release only what is checked and packed.
Dispatch controls with release sign-off, delivery challans and invoices.
h_stock: Make stock figures match the shelf
Record every issue and receipt when it happens, and count a few items every week instead of everything once a year.
Stores with bin cards, issues against work orders, stock counts and reorder alerts.
h_planning: Plan the week before it starts
A simple weekly plan by machine and order, reviewed every morning, removes most of the daily firefighting.
Production planning, job cards and machine efficiency (OEE).
h_cash: Review dues every week, oldest first, and note every promise to pay. Small habits shorten the cash cycle.
A collection worklist, ageing, promises to pay and a weekly cash-flow view.
h_accountability: Give every order and task a named owner and a date. Visible ownership does more than reminders.
Roles, approvals and each person’s own work list, with an audit log.
h_quality: Catch problems before the customer does
Inspect at receipt, during production and before dispatch, and record every rejection with its reason. Patterns show up quickly.
Inspections, test certificates and an NCR / CAPA register.
h_tenders: Keep every enquiry, quotation and tender in one list with its due date and next step, and review it weekly.
A tender and quotation pipeline with due dates, follow-ups and win rates.
